facts.text: De Soto was named after Spanish explorer Hernando de Soto, who first crossed the area in 1541.
The Crumpler‑Ferguson Log Cabin in De Soto has served as a Civil War field hospital, a way station on the Hernando Plank Road, a restaurant, and a home.
De Soto’s early growth began along the Chickasawhay River before the Mobile and Ohio Railroad, with housing possibly starting in 1845 and churches by 1858.
The DeSoto County Museum, located in De Soto, offers free daily tours and showcases artifacts that trace the county’s rich history.
An exhibit at the museum honors the memory of 1.5 million children who perished in the Holocaust, featuring black‑and‑white photographs and interactive images.
The museum also displays artifacts from DeSoto County’s early Jewish settlers, including a 2,000‑year‑old oil lamp from the Dead Sea and an 1880s bronze Menorah.
